clinical_notes: 5.7–6.4% = prediabetes; >=6.5% on two tests = diabetes; >=8.0% = poor glycaemic control. Primary diagnostic criterion per ADA.

label_2_critical: >= 126 mg/dL on two occasions (diabetes) OR < 55 mg/dL (severe hypoglycaemia)
clinical_notes: Must be fasting >= 8 hr. Hypoglycaemia alert: <70; significant: <54; severe: <40 mg/dL. For Indian pop. use same ADA cutoffs.
75 g oral glucose load. Most sensitive for early glucose intolerance. IGT = prediabetes. Done exactly at 2-hr mark post load.
Non-fasting. Alone can diagnose only if >= 200 + symptoms. Otherwise confirm with FPG or HbA1c.
Used to compute HOMA-IR = (fasting_glucose × fasting_insulin) / 405. HOMA-IR > 2.5 = insulin resistance; > 5.0 = severe. Very low in Type 1 DM.

label_2_critical: < 0.2 ng/mL (Type 1 DM / pancreatic failure) OR > 4.0 ng/mL
clinical_notes: Co-secreted with insulin in equimolar amounts. Low = Type 1 DM. Normal/high = Type 2 DM. Distinguishes T1 vs T2. Not in all lab panels; use if available.
Hypertriglyceridaemia is extremely common in T2DM and metabolic syndrome. Fasting sample required. >= 500 = immediate clinical concern.
Low HDL = independent CVD risk factor and metabolic syndrome criterion. ATP III cutoffs: <40 men / <50 women. Extremely common in T2DM.
ADA target: <100; <70 for high CVD risk diabetics. Friedewald equation: LDL = Total_Chol − HDL − (TG/5). Invalid if TG > 400.
ADA: screen all T2DM at diagnosis; all T1DM after 5 yr. Spot urine. Confirm on 2 of 3 samples over 3–6 months. Critical for diabetic kidney disease staging.
Calculated from serum creatinine using 2021 CKD-EPI equation (race-free). Screen annually in all diabetics. Decline = diabetic nephropathy progression.

label_1_mild: 25.0–34.9 kg/m² (overweight to obese — T2DM risk factor)
clinical_notes: Not a blood test but key T2DM risk factor. For South Asian population (incl. India): use adjusted cutoffs — >= 23 overweight; >= 25 obese (lower threshold due to higher metabolic risk at lower BMI).
Secondary feature. Dyslipidaemia is key comorbidity of T2DM. Provides context for CVD risk calculation alongside LDL, HDL, TG.

verified_source: WHO 2011 Technical Report: Haemoglobin Concentrations for Diagnosis of Anaemia (WHO/NMH/NHD/MNM/11.1)
clinical_notes: Primary diagnostic criterion. Mild=10–12.9(M)/10–11.9(F); Moderate=7.0–9.9; Severe=5.0–6.9; Life-threatening <5.0. Pregnant women: mild <11.0 g/dL.
Hematocrit ≈ 3× Hemoglobin value. Cross-check for anaemia. Hct < 21% typically requires transfusion. Part of standard CBC.
Low RBC = anaemia or blood loss. High RBC (>6.0M men/>5.5M women) = polycythaemia. Used with MCV to type anaemia.

label_2_critical: < 60 fL (severe microcytic; thalassaemia) OR >= 115 fL (severe macrocytic)
verified_source: WHO / NHANES / Clinical laboratory reference ranges
clinical_notes: Critical for anaemia typing: <80=microcytic (iron deficiency/thalassaemia); 80–100=normocytic (haemolysis/ACD); >100=macrocytic (B12/folate deficiency). Most important morphological marker. Present in Kaggle anemia dataset.
MCH = Hgb/RBC × 10. Low MCH = hypochromic = iron deficiency or thalassaemia. Closely correlated with MCV. In Kaggle anemia dataset.
MCHC = Hgb/Hct × 100. <30 = hypochromic (iron deficiency). >36.5 = hyperchromic (hereditary spherocytosis). Feature in Kaggle anemia dataset.

Measures RBC size variation. High RDW + low MCV = iron deficiency. High RDW + high MCV = B12/folate. Normal RDW + low MCV = thalassaemia (key differentiator). High RDW + normal MCV = mixed deficiency.

label_1_mild: 10–30 ng/mL (depleted iron stores — pre-latent iron deficiency)
label_2_critical: < 10 ng/mL (severely depleted — iron deficiency anaemia established)
clinical_notes: Best single test for iron stores. WHO threshold for iron deficiency: <12 ng/mL (children/women). NOTE: acute phase reactant — falsely ELEVATED in infection/inflammation even with iron deficiency. Confirm with serum iron + TIBC.
Diurnal variation; not reliable alone. Use with TIBC and ferritin. Low iron + high TIBC + low ferritin = iron deficiency confirmed. In ACD (anaemia of chronic disease): iron low but TIBC also low.
TIBC inversely reflects iron stores. High TIBC = iron deficiency. LOW TIBC = anaemia of chronic disease (ACD), malnutrition, or protein deficiency. Critical differentiator between IDA and ACD.
TSAT = (Serum Iron / TIBC) × 100. < 20% = functional iron deficiency. < 16% = traditional iron deficiency cutoff. Key in CKD anaemia management (KDIGO target: TSAT > 30% before ESA therapy).

label_1_mild: 150–299 pg/mL (borderline — grey zone; confirm with MMA/homocysteine)
label_2_critical: < 150 pg/mL (true B12 deficiency — megaloblastic anaemia risk)
verified_source: AHA / Endocrine Society / NHANES laboratory standards
clinical_notes: B12 deficiency → macrocytic megaloblastic anaemia + subacute combined degeneration of spinal cord. Very common in vegetarians/vegans and in India. Metformin depletes B12. Confirm with elevated MMA and homocysteine.

Folate deficiency → macrocytic anaemia WITHOUT neurological symptoms (unlike B12). Critical in pregnancy (neural tube defect prevention — target > 4.0). RBC folate > 180 ng/mL better long-term indicator.
Immature RBCs. Low = bone marrow not producing enough (IDA/B12/aplastic). High = compensating (haemolysis/bleeding recovery). KEY for differentiating hypoproliferative vs haemolytic anaemia.
Pancytopenia (low Hgb + low WBC + low PLT) = aplastic anaemia or haemolological malignancy. Low WBC in aplastic anaemia; elevated in infection-driven ACD. Important for anaemia type classification.
Thrombocytopenia + anaemia = aplastic anaemia / bone marrow failure / ITP / DIC / hypersplenism. Included in Kaggle anemia dataset. Pancytopenia detection requires all three CBC lines.
Primary CKD staging marker. CKD = eGFR < 60 for >= 3 months OR albuminuria >= 30 mg/g for >= 3 months. Use 2021 race-free CKD-EPI equation. Calculated from serum creatinine, age, sex.
Input for CKD-EPI eGFR equation. Affected by muscle mass (lower in elderly/women/malnourished → overestimates GFR). Use in conjunction with eGFR, not standalone.
BUN/Creatinine ratio: 10–20 = normal. > 20 = prerenal azotaemia (dehydration). < 10 = liver disease/malnutrition. Urea itself is 2.14× BUN value.
Albuminuria categories per KDIGO 2022: A1 (<30), A2 (30–300), A3 (>300). Combined with GFR for CKD risk staging. Spot urine (first morning void preferred). Confirm on 2 of 3 samples.

label_1_mild: >= 7.2 mg/dL men; >= 6.0 mg/dL women (hyperuricaemia — gout risk)
clinical_notes: Hyperuricaemia common in CKD (reduced renal excretion) and precipitates gout. Uric acid is nephrotoxic at high levels. Also elevated in metabolic syndrome, thiazide use, dehydration.

label_2_critical: < 3.0 g/dL (severe — poor CKD prognosis; nephrotic syndrome)
clinical_notes: Reflects hepatic synthetic function AND nutritional status. Low albumin in CKD = protein loss (nephrotic) + inflammation + malnutrition. Major prognostic marker in CKD. Also used in liver model.

label_1_mild: 3.0–3.49 (mild hypokalaemia) OR 5.1–6.0 (mild hyperkalaemia — common in CKD)
label_2_critical: < 2.5 (severe hypokalaemia; arrhythmia risk) OR > 6.0 (severe hyperkalaemia; cardiac arrest risk)
clinical_notes: Hyperkalaemia is one of the most dangerous CKD complications. eGFR < 45 → monitor K+ every 3 months. > 6.0 mEq/L = medical emergency. ACE inhibitors / ARBs + CKD raise K+ further.
Hyponatraemia common in advanced CKD (fluid retention). SIADH must be excluded. Rapid correction of hyponatraemia → osmotic demyelination syndrome. Correct slowly (< 8–10 mEq/L per 24 hr).
Metabolic acidosis is universal in advanced CKD due to reduced acid excretion. Bicarbonate < 22 mEq/L accelerates CKD progression and bone disease. KDIGO recommends supplementation when < 22.
Elevated in CKD due to reduced renal excretion. Causes secondary hyperparathyroidism, renal osteodystrophy, vascular calcification. Dietary phosphate restriction required > 4.5 mg/dL.

verified_source: KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD / Clinical laboratory reference ranges
clinical_notes: Correct for albumin: corrected Ca = measured Ca + 0.8 × (4.0 − albumin). Hypocalcaemia in CKD from reduced vitamin D + hyperphosphataemia. Must measure ionised calcium if albumin is low.

label_2_critical: < 8.0 g/dL (severe renal anaemia; ESA therapy indicated)
clinical_notes: Normocytic normochromic anaemia of CKD due to EPO deficiency (reduced production by diseased kidney). KDIGO: start ESA when Hgb < 10 g/dL in CKD. Target Hgb 10–11.5 g/dL with ESA. Exclude iron deficiency first.

Secondary hyperPTH = compensatory response to hypocalcaemia + hyperphosphataemia + low vitamin D in CKD. PTH target in dialysis patients: 2–9× upper limit of normal (KDIGO). Drives renal osteodystrophy.

label_1_mild: 130–189 mg/dL (borderline to high; Framingham risk elevated)
verified_source: AHA/ACC 2019 Guideline on Primary Prevention of CVD / ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guideline
clinical_notes: Primary CVD risk marker. Friedewald: LDL = Total_Chol − HDL − (TG/5); invalid if TG > 400 mg/dL — use direct LDL. Thresholds: <70 very high risk; <100 high risk; <130 moderate risk (AHA/ACC 2018).

label_2_critical: < 35 mg/dL (men); < 40 mg/dL (women) — very low (strong risk factor)
clinical_notes: HDL < 40 (men) / < 50 (women) = metabolic syndrome criterion. >= 60 mg/dL = negative risk factor (protective). HDL inversely correlates with CVD events. Elevated by exercise, moderate alcohol, niacin.
Input for Framingham and PCE (Pooled Cohort Equations) 10-year CVD risk score. TC alone not sufficient; use with LDL, HDL, TG. TC/HDL ratio > 5.0 is independent risk predictor.

label_1_mild: 150–499 mg/dL (borderline to high; independent CVD risk factor)
clinical_notes: Fasting sample. Elevated TG = metabolic syndrome, T2DM, hypothyroidism. TG 150–199 borderline; 200–499 high; >= 500 very high (chylomicronaemia + pancreatitis). At >400, Friedewald LDL formula invalid.
Calculated: Non-HDL = Total_Chol − HDL. Includes all atherogenic particles (LDL + VLDL + IDL + Lp(a)). Better predictor than LDL when TG > 200. Non-HDL target = LDL target + 30 mg/dL.

label_2_critical: > 3.0 mg/L (high CVD risk); > 10 = acute phase (rule out infection)
verified_source: AHA/ACC 2003 Scientific Statement on hsCRP / Reynolds Risk Score
clinical_notes: Inflammatory marker that independently predicts CVD events. JUPITER trial: statins reduced events in hsCRP > 2 + LDL < 130. If > 10 mg/L, repeat after 2 weeks to exclude acute infection/inflammation.
Each ApoB = one atherogenic lipoprotein particle. Better predictor of CVD than LDL-C especially when TG elevated or LDL-C discordant. European guidelines increasingly recommend ApoB over LDL-C.

label_1_mild: 30–50 mg/dL (borderline elevated; moderate CVD risk increase)
label_2_critical: > 50 mg/dL (high; independent strong CVD and ASCVD risk factor)
verified_source: EAS Consensus on Lp(a) 2022 / ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guideline
clinical_notes: Genetically determined; unaffected by diet. Measure once in lifetime. Elevated in >20% of South Asian population. New specific therapies (inclisiran, PCSK9i) are modestly effective. Convert nmol/L × 0.43 = mg/dL.

label_2_critical: > 30 µmol/L (severe — very high thrombosis + CVD risk)
verified_source: AHA / NHANES / European CVD Prevention Guidelines 2021
clinical_notes: Elevated by B12/folate/B6 deficiency, CKD, hypothyroidism, smoking. Treated with B vitamin supplementation. Common in vegetarians. Independently associated with CVD, stroke, and VTE.
Included as CVD risk factor. Diabetes = major independent CVD risk equivalent. Prediabetes already elevates CVD risk. Fasting glucose integrated into PCE risk calculator.
Not a blood test but most important modifiable CVD risk factor. Included in 10-year ASCVD risk (PCE) calculation. Measurement: 2+ readings on 2+ occasions. Target < 130/80 for high CVD risk patients.

MOST liver-specific transaminase. AASLD 2023 updated normal limits: 29–33 U/L men; 19–25 U/L women (lower than traditional 40 U/L). 3–10× ULN = moderate; >10× ULN = severe hepatitis (viral, autoimmune, ischaemic). ALT elevation pattern: >AST in viral/NAFLD; AST>ALT in alcoholic hepatitis.

label_2_critical: > 120 U/L (> 3× ULN — significant injury); > 1000 = ischaemic/toxic hepatitis
clinical_notes: Less liver-specific than ALT (also in cardiac/skeletal muscle). AST/ALT > 2 = alcoholic hepatitis. AST/ALT < 1 = NAFLD/viral hepatitis. Feature in UCI ILPD (Indian Liver Patient Dataset). Both required for comprehensive liver model.

label_1_mild: 148–440 U/L (1–3× ULN — cholestatic or bone disease)
label_2_critical: > 440 U/L (> 3× ULN — significant cholestasis / bone metastasis)
clinical_notes: Elevated mainly in cholestatic liver disease (PBC, PSC, bile duct obstruction) and bone disease (Paget, metastasis). NOTE: physiologically high in pregnancy and adolescent growth. Confirm liver origin with GGT (if GGT also high → liver source).

verified_source: NHANES / AASLD 2023 / Clinical laboratory reference ranges
clinical_notes: Highly sensitive for liver disease and alcohol use. GGT elevated in NAFLD, cholestasis, drug-induced liver injury, alcohol (most sensitive marker). Used to confirm ALP is of hepatic origin. Microsomal enzyme inducer (phenytoin, warfarin) elevates GGT without true liver disease.

verified_source: AASLD 2023 / NHANES / Clinical laboratory reference ranges
clinical_notes: Total = direct + indirect. In liver failure: ≥ 3 = MELD score component (mortality predictor). In haemolysis: indirect elevated. In bile duct obstruction: direct elevated. Gilbert syndrome: mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia (benign).

Elevated in hepatitis, cirrhosis, bile duct obstruction, Dubin-Johnson syndrome. Direct/Total ratio > 50% = conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia (hepatic/post-hepatic). < 20% = pre-hepatic (haemolysis). Feature in ILPD dataset.

label_2_critical: < 3.0 g/dL (severe; Child-Pugh score component; poor prognosis)
clinical_notes: Reflects hepatic synthetic function (half-life 20 days; responds slowly). Low in cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, malnutrition, protein-losing enteropathy. One of 5 Child-Pugh criteria (cirrhosis prognosis). Feature in UCI ILPD.

label_1_mild: 4.5–5.9 g/dL (mild low; malnutrition/liver disease) OR 8.4–10.0 (mild high)
verified_source: NHANES / AASLD / Clinical laboratory reference ranges
clinical_notes: Total protein = albumin + globulin. Low in liver failure + malnutrition. High in multiple myeloma (paraproteinaemia) or dehydration. A/G ratio (normal 1.2–2.2) used with total protein in UCI ILPD dataset.

label_1_mild: 0.8–1.19 (low A/G — chronic liver disease / autoimmune / infection)
label_2_critical: < 0.8 (reversed A/G — significant liver disease or gammopathy)
clinical_notes: A/G = Albumin / (Total Protein − Albumin). Reversal (<1.0) suggests reduced albumin production (liver disease) or increased globulin (chronic infection, autoimmune, multiple myeloma). Key feature in UCI ILPD (Indian dataset).

Clotting factor synthesis (II, VII, IX, X, protein C/S) depends on liver. PT prolonged in liver failure. INR = PT_patient/PT_control. MELD score uses INR. Child-Pugh: INR < 1.7 (1 pt); 1.7–2.3 (2 pts); > 2.3 (3 pts).

MELD = 3.78×ln(Bilirubin) + 11.2×ln(INR) + 9.57×ln(Creatinine) + 6.43. MELD > 15 = transplant evaluation. INR > 1.5 = coagulopathy requiring monitoring. Not affected by anticoagulants in this context.

verified_source: ATA 2023 Guidelines / Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline 2012
clinical_notes: TSH is the single most sensitive thyroid test. Pituitary TSH responds inversely to thyroid hormone levels. Most sensitive for early dysfunction. In pregnancy (first trimester) target TSH < 2.5 mIU/L. Elderly: upper limit may be higher (4.5–6.0).

label_1_mild: 0.5–0.79 ng/dL (low FT4 — hypothyroid) OR 1.9–2.9 ng/dL (mildly elevated)
verified_source: ATA 2023 / Endocrine Society 2012 / NHANES reference intervals
clinical_notes: Free (unbound) thyroxine — the active circulating form. Measured directly (immunoassay) rather than calculated. Required to distinguish overt vs subclinical dysfunction: TSH high + FT4 normal = subclinical; TSH high + FT4 low = overt hypothyroidism.

label_2_critical: < 1.5 pg/mL (overt hypothyroidism) OR >= 6.0 pg/mL (overt hyperthyroidism; T3 toxicosis)
clinical_notes: Most metabolically active thyroid hormone. FT3 elevated in early Graves disease and T3 thyrotoxicosis (FT3 rises before FT4). Also used in monitoring T3 replacement therapy. T3 toxicosis = TSH suppressed + FT4 normal + FT3 elevated.

Includes protein-bound + free T4. Affected by TBG changes (pregnancy, OCP increase TBG → raises total T4 but not free T4). Less reliable than FT4 for diagnosis. Use in conjunction with FT4 and TSH. Feature in UCI Thyroid dataset.
Most active thyroid hormone. T3 toxicosis: FT3 elevated with normal FT4. In severe illness: low T3 syndrome (euthyroid sick syndrome) — T4 → reverse T3 instead of T3. Feature in UCI Thyroid dataset.

label_2_critical: > 200 IU/mL (strongly positive; Hashimoto thyroiditis or Graves disease)
verified_source: ATA 2023 / Endocrine Society 2012 / AACE/ATA Thyroid Nodule Guidelines
clinical_notes: Elevated in 95% of Hashimoto thyroiditis (autoimmune hypothyroidism) and ~75% of Graves disease (autoimmune hyperthyroidism). Most useful antibody for autoimmune thyroid disease diagnosis. In euthyroid persons: elevated anti-TPO = 38× lifetime risk of developing hypothyroidism.

Elevated in 60–80% of Hashimoto and 50–70% of Graves. Less sensitive than anti-TPO for Hashimoto diagnosis. Critical for thyroid cancer monitoring: anti-TG interferes with thyroglobulin assay — must measure both.

label_1_mild: 18–23.9% (low — hypothyroid or increased TBG) OR 37.1–42.0% (mildly elevated)
label_2_critical: < 18% (overt hypothyroidism or very high TBG) OR > 42% (hyperthyroidism)
clinical_notes: Indirect measure of TBG binding capacity. Used to calculate Free Thyroxine Index (FTI = T4 × T3RU/100). FTI normal = 4.2–13.0. If direct FT4 available, T3RU is redundant. Present in older datasets (UCI Thyroid dataset).

label_1_mild: Context-dependent: post-thyroidectomy any detectable level = concerning
label_2_critical: > 100 ng/mL OR any detectable level post-thyroidectomy (cancer recurrence)
verified_source: ATA 2015 Management Guidelines for Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
clinical_notes: Primary use: thyroid cancer surveillance (tumour marker for papillary/follicular cancer). Undetectable post-thyroidectomy = complete remission. Rising level = recurrence. Anti-TG antibodies invalidate the assay. Not a routine thyroid function test.
